name: Price banner from frame 0
visual: The product (or the place) already moving, in a hand or in use, with a large price strip in the top third and the phone bar below; no intro.
examples: One bedroom In Gasogi Full furnished 400k / Month
Spinning bike / Price: 500k / Home workout Gym
Your next ride for only 50,000 RWF per day!

name: Promo for one price
visual: A hand unwraps or lifts the one product; the header text and the number stay up the whole clip.
examples: BEST BURGERS IN KIGALI / PROMO FOR 5K - DON'T MISS
hurry! hurry! special offer any style 1800 (inclusive of braids & free wash)
note: The longest-running local ad in the research (a Nairobi salon, 982 days) is this hook with one flat price that includes a free extra.

name: Was / now price anchor
visual: The product in use, a black bar on top with today's price; the old price crossed out beside it.
note: Only when the owner gives both prices. Pair a percentage with the real price so the saving feels concrete.

name: A price on every item
pattern: {product} {price} (one item every 2 s, each with its own label)
visual: A hand holds item after item in front of a wall of stock; a white or outlined price label rides on each one.

name: The whole price list in one frame
visual: One product in hand in front of a solid card listing every model and its price, the phone number at the bottom; it stays up.
examples: a printed MENU of nails and lashes: 1k to 7k, lashes 20k to 30k

name: Number on screen, product in hand
pattern: {phone} (top or lower-middle, whole clip) over {product} in a hand
visual: Hands turn the product to show front and back; the phone or WhatsApp number is fixed on screen from the first frame to the last.

name: Offer badge with the day
visual: Top-down table with the food; a solid badge with the offer and the day sits on screen for the whole clip.
examples: BUY ONE PIZZA GET ONE FREE EVERY TU
YOU GET ONE FREE EVERY TUESDAY
MONDAY - FRIDAY, 11 AM - 2 PM, LUNCH TIME Promo

name: Discount plus free delivery
visual: Shelf pans and one product held to the lens; the offer sits as a bottom-third card.
examples: 15% OFF regular prices + FREE DELIVERY in KGL.
note: Write free delivery only when the owner offers it.

name: Free, you only pay for ...
visual: The venue dressed and lit; the free things listed as ticks.
examples: Zana ibirori byawe kuri One Click Hotel ... aho kubikorera k'ubuntu na decoration k'ubuntu ... icyo usabwa nukwishyura ibyo kurya no kunywa gusa

name: POV: you just found ...
pattern: POV: You just found the most affordable {product} in {city}
visual: The shop front or the product in a hand, the POV line in big text at the top for the whole clip.
examples: POV: You just found the most affordable skincare vendor in Kigali
POV: Kenyan brands are stepping into global markets with our packaging
POV: You're about to make someone smile for just 15Tsh
POV: you're in Kigali, Rwanda... of course you're going to try the famous street food.
note: 'Most affordable' is a claim: use it only when the owner says so, else 'POV: you just found {product} in {city}'.

name: POV: the panic, then the rescue
visual: A relatable panic moment in 2 to 3 s (a guest is coming, nothing at home), then the product or service saves it.
examples: POV: She says “I’m close” and you have NOTHING at home
A BAD LUCK you don't wish

name: Me when ... (relatable text)
visual: One full-sentence line at the top, white bold, over a person reacting.
examples: Me after checking my result and realizing I passed despite all the nonsense I wrote in the exam.
I'm a small business owner but I'm also a...
when your business is small, EVERY order feels like a win
I'M A SMALL BIZ OWNER but I'm also a...
note: Seen on an entertainment clip (446K likes), not an ad: a format idea, keep it light and true.

name: Short direct question
visual: Two to four huge words with an outline, the person or product right behind; a second question can follow at 2 s.

name: Tired of ...? / Still ...?
visual: The everyday problem on screen first (dull, real), then a hard cut to the product fixing it.
examples: Tired of Snoring Ruining Your Sleep?
Nobody warns you how annoying juicers are to actually clean
Say goodbye to: Smudged polish, Chipped nails
Ready to see your skin exactly how it used to be?
Still dealing with razor bumps and ingrown hairs?
Still dealing with razor bumps and ingrown hairs?

name: Wait for it ... (the result first)
pattern: Wait for it... ({result} first, then the before)
visual: The finished result (the hairstyle, the room, the car) for 1 to 2 s with 'Wait for it...' or 'After', then the before.
examples: Shot and edited a beauty salon for a client. Wait for the end results...
note: Never a body, skin or medical before/after.

name: The product doing its job at second 0
pattern: (no words needed) {product} working in the first frame
visual: The job being done in one take: half a shirt smooth and half wrinkled, a blender running, a blade ejecting, a dress flap opening.
examples: Watch this stain lift in 8 seconds
note: The steamer demo (235.8K likes) has no on-screen text at all: the picture is the hook.

name: Appetite shot
pattern: {product} in macro: steam, a pull, a bite (price at the top)
visual: Food macro in the first second: steam, a cheese pull, a foil unwrap, a first bite by a real person.
examples: Fish lovers!! This is your time to enjoy muhazi tilapia fish !!
Mozzarella-stick cheese pull readable in under 1 s with no sound

name: Unwrap, open, reveal
visual: Top-down or POV hands: tape cut, lid lifted, the colour or the item is the reward.
examples: I’m absolutely in love with our new arrivals.
Our Mystery Box came packed with 9 amazing items

name: Now available / it's here
visual: The new item held up by real staff in front of real stock, or a flag and the product.
examples: Now available! Spinning Bikes Have Arrived in Kigali!
note: The cash-on-delivery sellers ran this template 7 to 12 variants for up to 24 months.

name: Where, what size, how much
visual: Three stacked labels (district, sector, street) over the first shot, then a pill with the rooms; the price follows.
examples: Ibibanza byiza Masaka inyuma Ya Gare Bigurishwa / Price: 16M

name: Whip pan into the tour
pattern: (a fast move into the best room or the view, the price in the title)
visual: A whip pan or a smooth gimbal glide into the best space at dusk; the caption carries the price.
examples: Touring An AMAZING Modern Luxury Custom Home in Frisco, Texas
$28,000,000 for a CASTLE in Las Vegas

name: Name and role card
visual: The expert in the real place (white coat, the classroom, the workshop) with a name and role card at second 0, boxed captions sentence by sentence.
examples: And I'm A Dermatologist Here At Derma Skin Clinic.
JUDITH SAFARIS | INGABIRE DORICE FINANCE & ADMINISTRATION OFFICER
The September intake is here, grab your seat now
note: Needs a real or digital-library presenter the owner chose; never invent a doctor or a title.

name: Greeting in Kinyarwanda
visual: A host (a shop assistant or the owner) walks the aisle and greets the camera; the price entry point and delivery line follow.
note: On-screen and caption only for Kinyarwanda: the voice model cannot speak it (owner rule, 17 October 2026).

name: Best / biggest in {city}
visual: The product huge in frame with the claim across the top.
examples: THE MOST CHEAPEST IPHONES IN KIGALI RWANDA IN 2026
The biggest Stainless Steel distributor in Nairobi from 30bob
note: Only the owner's own claim, word for word; never a superlative the engine made up.

name: Start your business with us
visual: A wall of stock, a worker packing, retail and wholesale written under the number.
examples: Start your cosmetics business with us
Start your Jewelry Business with Pieces_ug today.
If u want to start a business this video is for you
note: For wholesalers only. Never income promises.

name: Spec label per beat
visual: The seller holds the product (or the camera walks round it); one spec label per beat, in a white rounded box or a coloured tag: model, then the key specs.
examples: Drive system 4WD / 4x4 | Engine size 3,604 cc | Cylinders 6 (V6)

name: The rumours are true (cards in hand)
visual: A person holds paper cards up one by one; each card is one line of the announcement.

name: Reply to a customer's question
visual: A comment card on screen at 0 s (Do you deliver? Is this price real?), then the answer shown with proof.
examples: Is this price real? / Do you deliver?
note: Only a real question the owner received; never a made-up comment.

name: Happy customer
visual: A real customer opens, tries or eats it; the reaction is the proof.
note: Only real customers and their real words; a fictional presenter must not pose as one.

name: Numbered list
visual: Item 1 on screen at 0 s, one item per beat with a big number.
examples: Top 9 Best Secondary Schools in Rwanda

name: Don't say / Say
visual: A red wrong line and a green right line in one frame, the teacher pointing up at them.
note: 122K likes, the highest in the Facebook reels sample.

name: More than you think
pattern: Your {product} can do more than you think!
visual: The device's screen or a surprising feature in close-up.
examples: Your phone can do more than you think!

name: Occasion title over a grid
visual: A title card over four photos of the options, cross-fading; a 5 s loop is enough.
examples: Every Occasion Deserves The Flower Bar Touch!

name: We come to you
visual: Close-ups of the finished work alternating with a 2x2 grid of options; a bottom bar with the service and the number.
examples: airsalon Book Your Nails Home Service 0719-230-446

name: Episode of a series
visual: The same title card and layout every week, the new item or place inside it.
examples: How to Sell on Jumia Uganda (Step-by-Step Series)

name: Giant word behind the product
pattern: {product} (one huge word, cut by the frame edge, the product in front)
visual: The product floats in the middle with ingredients or particles around it; one giant word sits behind it and changes colour per beat.
examples: COOL DOWN WITH EVEREST BY SESKY

name: Macro detail under a rim light
pattern: (a detail of {product} in the dark, then the whole product, then the name)
visual: Beat 1 a gold cap or a label edge in macro with a rim light; beat 2 the product in a set with a slow orbit; beat 3 the name on a clean card.

name: One phrase per beat, one key word in colour
pattern: {claim} (2 to 4 words per beat, the key word highlighted)
visual: Words pop in with overshoot or stomp on the beat between solid frames; one word per phrase in the highlight colour.

name: Price pill pinned on every frame
visual: A rounded pill at the top with the plan and the price, on every frame; a person holding the product below and one benefit line per beat.
note: Piramie ran 6 variants of this template in 11 days: make several hero shots of the same layout.

name: Seller at the counter, price bar below
visual: The seller behind the shop counter holds the item up; a blue or yellow bar across the lower third with the product, the price and two numbers.
examples: TURN YOUR ROOM INTO A GALAXY
note: The bar sits above the app's bottom 15%.

name: Model name badge
visual: A yellow badge or sticker with the exact model over the boxes on the counter, or a hand fanning several phones.
examples: iPhone 18pro and 18pro max are available On discount
note: 'On discount' only when the owner gives the discount.

name: Kinyarwanda offer line
visual: One line in capitals over the product in use, the numbers in a bar below.
examples: KURI 38000FRW TUGUHA IYI TWO IN ONE SMARTWATCH
HA AHANTU HAWE ISURA YIHARIYE WIGURIRA INTEBE NZIZA KUGICIRO CYIZA
note: For Kinyarwanda businesses: written on screen and in the caption only (the voice speaks English). Use the owner's own wording when given.

name: Kigali, we need to talk
visual: The new product on a tray or counter, the line in big text, the logo small in a corner; then 'made fresh' proof shots.
note: 'First in Rwanda' is a claim: only the owner's.

name: Service claim in capitals, address on screen
visual: The service being done in close-up, the claim in capitals and a map pin with the landmark address at the bottom of the safe area.
examples: Kigali, Gacuriro KG 414 st, KG486st, Next to DELIGHT HOTEL

name: Stop losing ... (a loss or scare line)
visual: The problem in one bold line (a rusty railing, an empty shop page), then the fix and the free quote or consultation.
examples: Old railing rusting? Staircase looking tired?
note: For business-to-business services. No income promises.

name: How {product} changes your space
visual: The product transforms the scene in one move: a rug unrolls across the floor, a projector fills the ceiling with stars.
examples: How rugs can change your space !
Transform your space into pure luxury

name: Search bar question
visual: A search bar types the question over the product in close-up, then the answer in two or three short cards.
note: Skip the skin before/after this ad also shows.

name: Students or workers doing the work
visual: Hands on tools in the real workshop or classroom, matching uniforms; the branch numbers in the lower third.
examples: Master the skills of a professional mechanic

name: Poster first, then real clips
visual: A designed poster as the first frame: the offer or activity as the headline, a schedule block (days, times), the landmark, and a phone bar at the bottom; then 3 or 4 phone clips of the place.
examples: FRIDAY UNLOCKED / BUY 4 GET 5 / 6PM-10PM / KICUKIRO, KN 432 opposite IPRC traffic lights
EXPLORE THE WORLD / UP TO 35% OFF / BOOK NOW
HIKE MOUNT JALI WITH CAMP & EXPLORER | HIKING EVERY DAY MONDAY - SUNDAY | CONTACT US ON +250…

name: The product in a splash
pattern: (no words, or one) {product} hit by a splash or flying ingredients
visual: The can, bottle or tube in frame 0 with a splash or its ingredients flying round it on a colour that matches the label; the logo small.
examples: Fanta can with an orange splash
a lime soda can with flying lime slices
note: Draw the label and the price as text over the picture; never let a generated image write them.

name: Explode and reassemble
visual: The device floats on a dark floor glow, then its parts fly apart (screen, camera, battery) each with a two-word label, and lock back together.

name: Menu card loop
visual: A menu card with an 'ORDER NOW' button; the dish and its price slide to the next dish every 3 s and loop back.
examples: Super Delicious PIZZA | ORDER NOW | BBQ Chicken Pizza 470 $

name: Step 1, 2, 3 (one verb each)
visual: The product on a coloured circle with 'STEP 1' typing in; one verb per step (CLEANSE, TREAT, NOURISH), then the result close-up.

name: Open the door, walk the shop
visual: A hand pulls the door open into the bright shop; the shop name and the area on screen, then pans of the counter and the wall of stock.
examples: Jp mobiles and services | Duburi jajpur

name: Red price block beside the product
visual: A split card: the product picture on the left, the price in a red (or black and gold) block on the right; one card per model, the presenter or the real stock before and after it.
examples: Standard Eco Heater 40°C - 45°C | RWF 70,000 | Premium Rapid Heat | RWF 75,000

name: A key turns in the door
pattern: (a hand turns the key) {product} | from {price} a night
visual: POV: a hand turns a key in the wooden door, the door opens on the room; the phone strip at the bottom, the rates in the caption.
examples: Not A Hotel Room | Your Private Apartment

name: before... / after (one word each)
visual: The same framing twice: the old state with one lowercase word 'before...' held 2 to 3 s, a hard cut, the finished state with 'after' and a slow push-in.
note: Never a body, weight or face before/after: rooms, hair, shops and renovations only.

name: Something is missing (an empty frame, then the product)
pattern: {claim}! (over an empty space, then the products pop in)
visual: An empty shelf, vanity or room with one big line ('miss, you forgot something!'), or a 3, 2 countdown on black; then the products pop in or the room is revealed.

name: This is what {price} buys you
pattern: This is what {price} buys you in {city}
visual: The agent or owner walks towards the camera in front of the house or the stock; the line stacked in huge text, the price word coloured.
examples: This is what $10M just under buys you here in Lake Nona

name: The owner in front of the stock
visual: The owner or a staff member in a branded shirt talks to the camera over a spread of boxed stock, peeling the film off a phone or lifting the box.
examples: iPhone Pro Series Ka Buffet… 13 Pro to 16 Pro Max.

name: Trust and numbers first
visual: The place at its best (a lit pharmacy, the campus from above, the owner or a doctor in scrubs) with one line of trust numbers: the founding year, the branches, the insurers accepted, the schools taking part.
examples: First Private Pharmacy In Rwanda since 1969 | 6 Branches across Kigali
We work with EDENCARE, SONARWA, and RSSB
note: Only the numbers the owner gives; never an invented year, branch count or insurer.

name: One mannequin, a new colour every beat
visual: A locked shot of one mannequin or one pair of hands; the outfit swaps colour every 1 to 2 s while the number stays on screen for the whole clip.

name: The insurers you take
visual: The clinic or pharmacy at its best (the lit counter, the doctor in scrubs) with the insurers accepted written large for 2 to 3 seconds.
examples: We work with EDENCARE, SONARWA, and RSSB
note: Only the insurers the owner gives; viewers ask about them more than anything else on a clinic clip.
